Let's but that into: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/38329

We should fix it global and not partial. Feel like a endless bug hunting until we have a concept. I means that is nice (merge it into 38329 and use a global freeze on it). It's also a breaking change with should not go into a bugfix release. Let's cooking a stable core for 0.114 on 38329 which is aware of all that issues.

Update: Maybe we should not merge it into my timeout PR. But while I work on that, I remember me better on `async_add_entities` which can not block itself. Yes that function can block but because of force updates or blocking async overwrites (we can't protect for everything). I think more usefully would be to protect the force update for blocking forever. I'm not sure if this is the right place for that code in general. Maybe @balloob see that different - I see no issue with this code but we should not put it into a bugfix release before we tested it on dev

It looks like it hanging calling `_async_add_entity` in:

in homeassistant.helpers.entity_platform.EntityPlatform.async_add_entities
```
        tasks = [
            self._async_add_entity(  # type: ignore
                entity, update_before_add, entity_registry, device_registry
            )
            for entity in new_entities
        ]

        # No entities for processing
        if not tasks:
            return

        await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
```

Likely the only thing that can block there is

```
                await entity.async_device_update(warning=False)
```
OR
```
        await entity.async_internal_added_to_hass()
        await entity.async_added_to_hass()
```
